findings.title: The S3 transcript refetch in `adoptAcceptedTurn` survives the entire OperatorClient suite — no case can see the second message in an already-adopted conversation
findings.reason: Raised in round 3, inside the round-3 scope (it is B1-16's own target line). M-B16 removed `setReloadEpoch((value) => value + 1)` from `adoptAcceptedTurn` (useOperatorConversation.ts:354) and B1-16 PASSED; the full file then ran under the same mutant and ALL 16 cases passed. Two measurements, both recorded. Why B1-16 cannot see it: that case sends the FIRST message of a NEW conversation, so the same callback also moves `setConversationId(null -> CONVERSATION)` and `setFresh(true -> false)`, each a dependency of the load effect (useOperatorConversation.ts:335), and the read re-runs without the epoch bump. Why nothing else sees it: reverse import search — `useOperatorConversation` is imported only by `OperatorClient.tsx`, `useProposalWrites.ts` and `useTurnPoll.ts`; `useProposalWrites.test.tsx` passes `patchProposal` / `reloadTranscript` in as `vi.fn()` so the real hook is never reached; the only suite that renders `OperatorClient` is `OperatorClient.test.tsx`. The one case that does send a second message in an ALREADY-adopted conversation (`terminal failures and requested capabilities survive reload and subsequent turns`, OperatorClient.test.tsx:646-687) asserts only that the EARLIER cards stay, never that the new owner text appears — which is the assertion the refetch exists for, and its conversation GET answers a fixed two-turn body that could not carry a third turn anyway. This is NEW production behaviour, not an old front: `useOperatorConversation.ts` is +415/-0 against the merge base `6edacd0b0`, and the merge-base `OperatorClient.tsx` contains no `setReloadEpoch` at all. The code comment at :349-353 records the regression it fixed in its own words ("the owner's own words were on no part of the screen for the twenty to sixty seconds the turn takes (S3)"), so the property matters and production at HEAD is correct. Severity P2, matching this sidecar's own calibration for "the line is executed but no assertion discriminates it, and HEAD is not defective" — RT-B7 and RT-B6 were both recorded P2 on that basis at the round-2 close; it is deliberately NOT the protocol's "uncovered change" P1, which is a production hunk with NO covering candidate, whereas two cases execute this line. Elevation to P1 is the owner's call and would block the PR. Remedy, one case and a fixture line: in the subsequent-turns case, let the conversation GET answer a THIRD stored turn carrying the second message's text and assert it is on screen after the second send — that text can reach the transcript only through the refetch `adoptAcceptedTurn` asks for, since the composer empties on send and there is no optimistic bubble.

The mutant is NOT behaviour-preserving in production: a second message in an already-adopted conversation would leave the transcript showing only the previous exchange for the life of the turn. It is therefore not recorded as `equivalent` at the file level. It is also not a `survived-confirmed-P0`: a P0 is a proven-fake test or a correctness defect, and HEAD is correct — what is missing is an assertion, which is the P1/P2 band. Within that band the distinguishing fact is that the protocol's P1 "uncovered change" means a hunk with no covering test, and this hunk has two covering cases, so it is recorded at P2 with the elevation argument stated for the owner rather than silently chosen.
